newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to idle light truck plants Friday.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to idle light truck plants Friday.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Thursday it will halt production at four light truck plants starting tomorrow because of a strike by 1,800 members of the United Auto Workers union at a company engine plant here.

Chrysler spokesman Tony Cervone said the idling will affect light truck assembly workers at the automaker's Dodge City plant in Warren, Mich.; Jefferson North plant in Detroit; St. Louis Assembly North; and the Pillette Road full-size van assembly plant in Windsor, Ontario.

The plants will be idled after they finish production scheduled for today. The plants make some of Chrysler's hottest-selling and most profitable vehicles, including the Dodge Ram and Dakota pickup trucks and Jeep Grand Cherokee sport/utility vehicle.

Workers from Chrysler's Mound Road engine plant in Detroit struck early this morning after contract talks broke down over staffing and outsourcing issues. The plant supplies various versions of V-6, V-8 and V-10 engines for Chrysler light trucks.
Cervone said no new negotiations are scheduled for today.
